QA REVIEW #2 (qa-f0a7b13f) — APPROVE at HEAD e53b8b810a107c8bf9de3e6a6f295ea4134d9f6f. The rejected clause is fixed at the production surface and the arm that was missing now demonstrably catches the exact defect that shipped.

THE REJECTED DEFECT IS GONE — my own independent probe, not the worker's. `node --experimental-strip-types` importing `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` from packages/contracts/src/index.ts returns `{"len":96,"isSorted":true,"firstMismatch":null,"idx":55,"prev":"policy.validate","next":"profile.register","unique":true}`. At the rejected commit the same shape of probe returned `isSorted:false` with `firstMismatch {i:55, actual:'profile.register', expected:'product_contract.approve_gate_1'}`. Whole tuple sorted, kind unique, position correct by neighbour.

THE NEW ARM BINDS — I re-ran the decisive drill myself rather than reading the worker's B2 transcript. Mutation: swapped the pair back to `"profile.register", "product_contract.approve_gate_1"` in BOTH packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts AND the hand roster in runtime-contract.test.ts — i.e. exactly the state that shipped in 5ff4e396 and passed every gate. Result: `× keeps every command kind at its sorted position`, `Tests 1 failed | 11 passed (12)`, EXIT 1, with the diagnostic `{ actual: 'profile.register', expected: 'product_contract.approve_gate_1', index: 55 }`. Only that arm redded; the hand-roster `toEqual` arm stayed green, which is the proof that the new assertion covers what the roster structurally cannot. Prestate porcelain empty; backups in %TEMP%; restore in a separate call; separate proof call: vocabulary SHA256 09064228...ED90C0 and test SHA256 E90B25E6...3EE175 both equal their backups, `git diff --exit-code` exit 0, `packages/contracts/` porcelain empty.
On the arm's shape: `[...RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS].sort()` is derived from the module under test, but sortedness is a self-comparison property by definition, so this is not a fixed point — the drill above is the evidence, since a wrong order makes the two differ and reds. The neighbour pins (`policy.validate` / `profile.register`) add the per-kind fence without hard-coding an absolute index.

DIGEST / REGENERATION, verified rather than accepted. I ran `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` myself: EXIT 0 with the executed echo `$ node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`, and `git diff --exit-code -- packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts` afterwards is exit 0. So regeneration really is byte-stable across the reorder (the generator sorts before emitting and before digesting), and the worker's "no rotation was due" is a measured fact, not an assumption. `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` remains 76d8404867d15b3b..., the kind is present in the generated client, and `git grep -c f110723782b6f8f9c5b3c976e3ecc1549167b448374d496f16e30ba8c873c23a HEAD` (the pre-5ff4e396 digest) returns ZERO hits.

GATES RE-RUN BY ME, each standalone with nonzero count lines:
- Recorded verification verbatim: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-schemas.test.ts` -> EXIT 0, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 30 passed (30)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/contracts/src/runtime` -> EXIT 0, 2 files / 70 tests.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` -> EXIT 0, 7 files / 57 tests; `typecheck` -> EXIT 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test` -> EXIT 0, 11 files / 216 tests.
- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts` -> EXIT 0, 1 file / 56 tests (release admission still accepts the digest).
- `pnpm typecheck:release` -> EXIT 0 with the full `$ tsc --noEmit --strict ...` echo naming release-subject.mjs.
- Root `pnpm test`, START_HEAD = END_HEAD = e53b8b81 -> EXIT 0, `Test Files 373 passed | 2 skipped (375)`, `Tests 9299 passed | 46 skipped (9345)`, zero FAIL lines.

RAILS. The commit is 2 files / 30 insertions / 2 deletions by explicit pathspec — runtime-vocabulary.ts (one line) and runtime-contract.test.ts — with NO apps/daemon file touched, and `git grep -c '"product_contract.approve_gate_1"' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src` returns zero, so the daemon still refuses the kind by absence of a registry handler exactly as DoD 5 requires; the probe pinning INPUT_INVALID at stage REGISTRY has its full source recorded in comment-08a9b971 and was re-run on the reordered tuple. Consumers named by id in the row's comments: task-7997ba7cefe542698d5a8078dbe56283 (P2.10a-ii) and task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591. The one owned-path collision (scripts/release/release-subject.mjs, task-a9c6d4a5) is moot: this re-entry rotated no mirror and the file is untouched and clean.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The kind is published on its own so the daemon writer (P2.10a-ii) can gate on it at HEAD; landing the daemon entry first would name a kind the contract refuses. REJECTED: hand-editing generated-client.ts — generator-determinism.test.ts:38 requires byte equality with a fresh emit. REJECTED: deriving the runtime-contract count from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length — the test's own header explains a duplicated member shrinks the set only; the literal moves 95 → 96. REJECTED: leaving release-subject.mjs to task-a9c6d4a5 unconditionally — whether it is still a hand mirror depends on landing order, so step 1(c) measures and the plan branches on the measurement. REJECTED: adding a daemon test for the fail-closed refusal — the row's rail forbids apps/daemon edits; a disposable probe with its source in the comment is the admissible evidence form. Name chosen: `product_contract.approve_gate_1` (label `product_contract_approve_gate_1`), following the underscore-segment precedent of `safe_boundary.observe`; injectivity is proven by the existing stdio-schemas arm plus the new per-kind arm.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured 2026-08-27 at HEAD cccf133e. RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-111) is a sorted `as const` tuple of 95 kinds; runtime-contract.test.ts pins a hand-transcribed EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS (`toEqual`, order-sensitive) and `commands.size === 95` (:98-100). ce426b93 (events.resume) touched exactly five files: vocabulary, runtime-contract.test.ts (list + 94→95), generated-client.ts (regenerated), generated-coverage.test.ts (GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 + CONTRACT_DIGEST), stdio-schemas.test.ts (per-kind arm). generator: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` = `node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`; generator-determinism.test.ts:23/:38/:51 pins repeat-emit equality, committed-equals-fresh, LF only. Digest mirrors at cccf133e (memory generated-contract-digest-has-four-mirrors): generated-client.ts:885, generated-coverage.test.ts:36 (`CONTRACT_DIGEST`; `GENERATED_FILE_SHA256` at :35 = 653339dd…), scripts/release/release-subject.mjs:56, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18. Release admission path: client-compat.ts:169 compares the manifest's contractSchemaHash to GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS.contractDigest; release-subject.mjs:184 refuses CONTROL_ROOM_COMPATIBILITY_REFUSED; distribution-packaging.test.ts (56 tests) uses GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS.contractDigest as SCHEMA_HASH. task-a9c6d4a5 (WORKING) will make release-subject.mjs derive the digest — landing order decides whether :56 is in this row's rotation set. The daemon wires a SUBSET of the vocabulary (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts PAYLOAD_KEYS keyed by WiredCommandKind); unwired members are refused at the seam.
planningNotes.risks: Missing one mirror silently breaks clean release admission (this happened twice: 46ae996, ce426b93) — the zero-hit grep of the OLD digest AT THE COMMIT is the guard, not a worktree grep. apps/control-room's tree is dirty with foreign WIP; only data-adapter.test.ts is owned and it must be clean before editing. The generated file's hash pin must be recomputed from the committed bytes (LF only). Do not touch apps/daemon; if the probe shows the daemon accepting the kind, stop and report. Sorted position matters for the order-sensitive `toEqual`.

issues.description: The new kind is after profile.register, but ordinal/JavaScript lexical order is policy.* -> product_contract.* -> profile.* -> project.*. Independent production probe returned isSorted:false with first mismatch at index 55: actual profile.register, expected product_contract.approve_gate_1. Move product_contract.approve_gate_1 before profile.register.

The hand-transcribed expectation repeats the same unsorted order, so all tests remain green while DoD 2 is violated. Correct the roster order and add an explicit sorted-order assertion against the production RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (retain the independent literal roster/count), then rerun regeneration/determinism and every required focused gate.

rejectionHistory.reason: REJECTED on the explicit sorted-position clause of DoD 2. Delivered commit 5ff4e396 otherwise passed independent gates (exact task verification 2 files/29 tests; contracts 2/69; client 7/57 plus typecheck; MCP 11/216; distribution 1/56; app adapter 1/16; typecheck:release; repo 372 passed + 1 skipped / 9284 passed + 44 skipped) and the digest mirror mutation reddened the named golden. However, a direct production probe over RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS exited 1: {isSorted:false, firstMismatch:{actual:'profile.register', expected:'product_contract.approve_gate_1', i:55}}. The roster test duplicates that wrong order and therefore does not detect the violation. Move the kind before profile.register in both production and the hand roster, add a durable sorted-order assertion, regenerate (even if byte-stable), and rerun the task gates.
